newsitem.title: USA: CBOT grain/soycomplex closing snapshot - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: CBOT grain/soycomplex closing snapshot - Jan 2.

text.p: WHEAT - Ended 9-3/4 to three cents per bushel higher, aided by spillover strength from the soy complex. Talk that Egypt will tender soon for 500,000 tonnes of wheat was also supportive. Pit sources said Paine Webber sold around 4.0 million bushels of March on the day.

CORN - Finished 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 1/2 cent higher. Concern about impact of heat in Argentina on that country's corn crop was supportive although impact partly offset by talk that a leading private analytical firm will issue a bearish crop estimate on Friday. Pit sources said Cargill bought 6.0 million bushels March on the day while Paine Webber sold 10.0 million bushels March.

SOYBEANS - Ended 8-1/2 to 11-1/4 cents per bushel higher on short covering by commodity funds. Pit sources said funds bought at least 20 million bushels on the day. Paine Webber and Smith Barney bought around 6.0 million bushels each. There was also talk a leading private analytical firm would issue a bullish crop estimate on Friday.

SOY PRODUCTS - Soyoil ended up 0.25 to 0.34 cent per lb while soybean meal finished $3.00 to $5.00 per ton higher. Pit sources said funds bought at least 3,000 lots of meal and 1,000 lots of oil on the day.
News that U.S. Food and Drug Administration was proposing to ban ruminant tissue use in animal feed for ruminant animals also supportive to soymeal.
